title: Table Freshness Anomaly Detection
dataSources: Monte Carlo incident webhooks (`montecarlo:incident`), Great Expectations `validation_result` JSON (`great_expectations:validation`), Soda scan results (`soda:scan`), dbt test failures, warehouse `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` freshness/volume probes via DB Connect.
app: Monte Carlo / Bigeye / Soda webhooks and REST APIs via HEC; Great Expectations and dbt test results via HEC scripted inputs; custom warehouse data-quality probes via Splunk DB Connect.
spl:
index=dataops sourcetype=dbx:warehouse_freshness
| stats latest(last_loaded_epoch) as last_load by database, table_name
| eval hours_since=round((now()-last_load)/3600,1)
| where hours_since>24
| sort - hours_since
description: Probes the warehouse for the last load time of each monitored table and flags tables that have not updated within their expected window, the core freshness check of data observability.
value: Stale tables are the most common cause of wrong dashboards; freshness monitoring catches data that stopped updating before anyone builds a decision on it.
implementation: Run a scheduled DB Connect query against `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`/metadata for max load timestamps; schedule hourly; set per-table thresholds via a lookup; alert on breaches.
visualization: Table of stale tables by hours-since-load, freshness heat map, alert.
grandmaExplanation: We check that the data behind your reports is being refreshed on time, so nobody makes a decision on numbers that quietly stopped updating.
